source_caption:
Anne Hathaway & Jim Sturgess in ‘One Day’ (2011) ❤️‍🩹

One Day (2011), directed by Lone Scherfig and based on the novel by David Nicholls, tells a long, bittersweet love story that unfolds one day at a time. The film follows Emma and Dexter, played by Anne Hathaway and Jim Sturgess, whose lives stay connected over the years after meeting on the night of their college graduation.

Instead of showing every moment, the story checks in with them on the same date each year, July 15th, letting the audience watch how their friendship shifts, grows, and sometimes falls apart as life takes them in different directions. Emma dreams of becoming a writer and building a meaningful life, while Dexter chases success and fame, often making choices that pull him further away from the person he used to be. Reviews often pointed out that this structure gave the film a reflective, almost nostalgic tone, showing how quickly time passes and how small decisions shape entire lives.

One interesting detail from production is that the film was shot in multiple real locations across the UK and Europe to capture the passage of time realistically, including Edinburgh, where their story begins. Critics had mixed reactions to the film, but many praised Hathaway’s emotional performance and the way the story explores friendship, missed chances, and timing in relationships.

At its core, One Day is about timing, growing up, and the quiet realization that love isn’t always about dramatic moments. Sometimes it’s about the years you spend circling back to the same person, only to realize how much they’ve meant to you all along.

source_details.synopsis: One Day is a 2011 romantic drama film directed by Lone Scherfig from a screenplay by David Nicholls, based on Nicholls' 2009 novel of the same name. It stars Anne Hathaway and Jim Sturgess, with Patricia Clarkson, Ken Stott and Romola Garai in supporting roles. It was released in the United States on 19 August 2011 by Focus Features and in the United Kingdom on 24 August 2011 by Universal Pictures. After meeting and spending the night together on St. Swithun's Day on the eve of their college graduation, Dexter and Emma are shown each year over 20 years on this same date.
